note: Names, centres and diameters from the IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature (USGS). Map coordinates converted to south polar stereographic (R = 1737.4 km).

places.name: Shackleton
places.namesake: Sir Ernest Henry; Irish-born British Antarctic explorer (1874-1922).
places.fact: Its rim almost touches the south pole. The crater floor has been in permanent shadow for billions of years.

places.name: Cabeus
places.fact: In October 2009 NASA crashed the LCROSS probe into this crater and detected water in the plume.

places.name: Mons Mouton
places.fact: Intuitive Machines' Athena lander (IM-2) touched down near here in March 2025.

places.name: Nobile
places.fact: Target region of Astrobotic's Griffin Mission One.

places.name: Faustini
places.fact: A crater whose floor never sees the Sun.

places.name: Haworth
places.namesake: Sir Walter Norman; English chemist, 1937 Nobel Prize winner for chemistry (1883-1950).
places.fact: A large permanently shadowed crater; NASA lists Haworth among its candidate landing regions.

places.name: Shoemaker
places.fact: NASA's Lunar Prospector, carrying some of Eugene Shoemaker's ashes, was crashed into this crater in 1999.

places.name: de Gerlache
places.fact: Its rim is one of NASA's candidate regions for crewed landings.

places.name: Mons Malapert
places.fact: A large massif with a clear line of sight toward Earth.

places.name: Amundsen
places.fact: A 100 km crater named after Roald Amundsen, first to reach Earth's South Pole.

places.name: Lacus Tenebrarum
places.fact: "Lake of Darkness": a low, shadowed plain.
